tasks.question: How does the TextArea.get_text() method's delegation pattern to self._text.get_text() enable framework-agnostic text retrieval while maintaining compatibility with matplotlib's text rendering API?
tasks.reference_answer: TextArea owns a matplotlib.text.Text child and uses Matplotlib transforms for layout (lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py:735-744). get_text simply forwards to that child, keeping text storage and retrieval consistent with Text rather than duplicating it (lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py:746-753). This abstracts the contained Text from callers; it does not make TextArea independent of Matplotlib or universally interchangeable with other frameworks.

tasks.question: Why does the RendererSVG class employ a deferred rendering strategy where clip paths and hatches are written only during finalization rather than immediately when encountered?
tasks.reference_answer: RendererSVG caches clip and hatch definitions by property keys, returning existing identifiers for repeat encounters (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_svg.py:494-511,605-626). finalize emits both dictionaries before closing the SVG (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_svg.py:344-348). _write_clips and _write_hatches each create their own defs section (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_svg.py:513-519,628-649). This batches cached definitions and avoids duplicates; a single shared defs section is not the implementation.

tasks.question: Why does the FigureCanvasPS class reconcile the dual rendering pathways between _print_figure and _print_figure_tex to maintain consistent PostScript output quality while accommodating both standard and TeX-based text rendering modes?
tasks.reference_answer: FigureCanvasPS._print_ps chooses _print_figure_tex when text.usetex is enabled, otherwise _print_figure, passing shared output options (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_ps.py:995-1000). Both use MixedModeRenderer; the TeX route converts PSFrag placeholders through its external TeX pipeline (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_ps.py:1044-1047,1157-1160,1202-1214). The common interface supports different text-rendering mechanisms; it does not itself guarantee identical typography, quality, or timing.

tasks.question: Why does the repeated instantiation of figure and axes objects with different DPI values in test_legend_proper_window_extent impact renderer caching and what performance degradation occurs when get_window_extent is called sequentially on legends without renderer state reuse?
tasks.reference_answer: Each Agg canvas caches RendererAgg by width, height and dpi, creating it when the key changes (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_agg.py:388-395). Figure._get_renderer directly calls canvas.get_renderer when available (lib/matplotlib/figure.py:2849-2852), so repeated legend extent queries do not require prior canvas.draw or trigger full drawing on Agg. The fallback captures a renderer by immediately aborting a patched draw (lib/matplotlib/backend_bases.py:1589-1618). Separate figures have separate caches, but this test does not quantify a performance degradation.

tasks.question: How does TransformWrapper's set() method maintain invalidation state consistency when replacing a child transform, and what is the significance of the double invalidation pattern with _invalid flag reset?
tasks.reference_answer: TransformWrapper.set invalidates using the old child state, checks dimensional compatibility, removes the old parent link, attaches the new child and rebinds delegated methods (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:1743-1771). It then resets _invalid, invalidates with the new child in place, and resets again (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:1776-1778). invalidate chooses affine-only versus full invalidation from is_affine, rather than copying a child invalid flag (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:154-176). Thus ancestors are notified around a possible change in transform type while the delegating wrapper ends with _invalid=0.
